reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the formation of Hf-rich precipitates at interfaces, the hindrance of grain-boundary sliding and dislocation motion, and the improvement in high-temperature strength at 0.5 at.% Hf, while also confirming unchanged room-temperature performance. However, the specific quantitative strength improvement (to >800 MPa) and the claim about unchanged density are not explicitly stated in the cited passage, representing minor overstatements.
premises: Hf addition (~0.5 at.%) forms fine Hf-rich precipitates at interphase boundaries
These precipitates hinder grain-boundary sliding and dislocation motion at high temperature
This improves high-temperature yield strength (e.g., from ~474 MPa to >800 MPa)
Alloy density is not significantly increased
